title: AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional (DOP-C02) practice questions

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A team stores code in GitHub and wants AWS CodePipeline to start automatically on every push to the main branch. What should it configure?
options: A source action that uses an AWS CodeConnections (formerly CodeStar Connections) connection to the GitHub repository
A personal access token stored in the pipeline's environment variables
An S3 bucket that developers upload zip files to manually
A CloudWatch alarm on the repository
questions.correct_rationale: CodeConnections authorizes CodePipeline to watch the repository and trigger on pushes.
questions.distractor_summary: Plain-text tokens are insecure, manual uploads are not automatic, and alarms do not watch Git repositories.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A pipeline deploys to accounts for dev, test, and prod. Build artifacts are encrypted. Deployments to the prod account fail with access denied when reading artifacts. What is the most likely fix?
options: Use the default AWS managed key for S3, which works across accounts
Copy artifacts to the prod account by email
Use a customer managed KMS key for the artifact bucket and grant the prod account's deployment role permission to use the key and read the bucket
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-account pipelines need a customer managed key whose key policy allows the other accounts' roles, plus bucket access.
questions.distractor_summary: Public buckets are unsafe, AWS managed keys cannot be shared across accounts, and email is not a deployment mechanism.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: In AWS CodeBuild, which file defines build phases, commands, and artifacts?
questions.correct_rationale: The buildspec file lists install, pre_build, build, and post_build commands plus artifacts.
questions.distractor_summary: appspec.yml is for CodeDeploy, template.yaml is typically a SAM or CloudFormation template, and a Dockerfile builds images.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A company wants production deployments to pause until a release manager approves them, with an email notification. What should be added to CodePipeline?
options: A CodeBuild project that sleeps for 24 hours
A manual approval action with an SNS topic for notifications
A Lambda function that always fails
A CloudFormation stack with no resources
questions.correct_rationale: Manual approval actions stop the pipeline until someone approves or rejects, and can notify through SNS.
questions.distractor_summary: Sleeping builds waste money, failing functions break the pipeline, and empty stacks do nothing.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: Builds take 20 minutes because dependencies are downloaded every time. How can build time be reduced in CodeBuild?
options: Enable local or S3 caching for dependency directories in the build project
Run builds only once per week
questions.correct_rationale: Caching dependencies avoids repeated downloads between builds.
questions.distractor_summary: Smaller compute slows builds, removing tests reduces quality, and weekly builds slow feedback.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: Which CodePipeline feature lets one pipeline run actions in parallel within the same stage?
options: Assigning the same run order to multiple actions in a stage
Using a manual approval between every action
Using separate pipelines for each action
questions.correct_rationale: Actions with the same runOrder value in a stage run in parallel.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate stages or approvals run sequentially, and separate pipelines lose coordination.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A team wants pipeline changes reviewed like application code. What practice fits best?
options: Edit the pipeline in the console whenever needed
Let any developer change the pipeline without review
Document the pipeline in a slide deck
Define the pipeline itself as infrastructure as code, such as CloudFormation or CDK, stored in version control
questions.correct_rationale: Pipelines as code are versioned, reviewed, and reproducible.
questions.distractor_summary: Console edits and unreviewed changes drift, and slides are not executable definitions.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A monorepo contains several services. The team wants a pipeline to run only when files for a specific service change. Which feature supports this?
options: A V1 pipeline with polling every minute
A CloudWatch metric filter on commits
CodePipeline V2 triggers with file path filters on the Git source
A manual approval at the start of each pipeline
questions.correct_rationale: V2 pipelines support trigger filters such as branches and file paths.
questions.distractor_summary: Polling runs on every change, metric filters do not start pipelines, and approvals do not filter changes.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: What is the main purpose of AWS CodeArtifact in a CI/CD workflow?
options: Hosting private package repositories and proxying public ones such as npm and PyPI
questions.correct_rationale: CodeArtifact stores and shares software packages with access control.
questions.distractor_summary: Tests run in CodeBuild, CloudFormation deploys stacks, and container images live in Amazon ECR.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A company wants every pipeline execution's source revision, build ID, and deployment result recorded for audit. What provides this most directly?
options: Developers writing notes after each deployment
CodePipeline execution history together with CloudTrail events and EventBridge notifications stored centrally
Disabling pipeline logs to save cost
A single CloudWatch dashboard with CPU metrics
questions.correct_rationale: Execution history and events give an automatic record of what ran and when.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual notes are unreliable, disabling logs removes evidence, and CPU metrics do not record releases.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: Builds need access to a private database in a VPC to run integration tests. How should CodeBuild be configured?
options: Configure the build project with VPC settings, private subnets, and a security group that the database allows
Run integration tests on developer laptops only
Store the database in the build container
questions.correct_rationale: CodeBuild can run inside a VPC to reach private resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Public databases are risky, laptop-only testing skips the pipeline, and an in-container database is not the shared test database.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A team wants to stop a deployment if unit test coverage drops below 80 percent. Where should this check run?
options: In the load balancer health check
In the CodeBuild test stage, failing the build when the coverage report is below the threshold
questions.correct_rationale: Failing the build early prevents low-quality changes from progressing.
questions.distractor_summary: Production and monthly checks are too late, and health checks do not measure coverage.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: Which CodeBuild feature displays test results, such as pass rates and trends, from JUnit or Cucumber reports?
questions.correct_rationale: Report groups collect test results and show trends over time.
questions.distractor_summary: Batch builds run builds in parallel, webhooks trigger builds, and environment variables configure builds.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A company wants to run integration tests against a fully deployed copy of the stack for every change, then tear it down. Which pipeline design fits best?
options: Skip integration tests to save time
Deploy an ephemeral test stack with CloudFormation, run tests in CodeBuild, then delete the stack in a later action
Keep one permanent shared test stack edited by hand
questions.correct_rationale: Ephemeral stacks give isolated, repeatable integration tests.
questions.distractor_summary: Testing in production risks users, skipping tests reduces quality, and hand-edited shared stacks drift.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: Before a canary deployment shifts more traffic, the team wants to run automated smoke tests against the new version. How can CodeDeploy support this for Lambda?
options: Use BeforeAllowTraffic and AfterAllowTraffic hooks to invoke validation functions
Use a manual approval in CodeBuild
questions.correct_rationale: CodeDeploy Lambda deployments support validation hooks that can fail the deployment.
questions.distractor_summary: EC2 lifecycle hooks and S3 events do not apply here, and CodeBuild has no manual approval action.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: Which type of testing checks that a change does not break existing functionality?
questions.correct_rationale: Regression tests rerun existing tests to confirm previous behavior still works.
questions.distractor_summary: Load, chaos, and penetration tests check performance, resilience, and security.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: Security wants every container image scanned for vulnerabilities before deployment. What fits best in the pipeline?
options: Enable Amazon ECR enhanced scanning with Amazon Inspector and fail the pipeline on critical findings
Trust that base images are always secure
Scan only after deployment to production
questions.correct_rationale: Scanning in the pipeline blocks vulnerable images before release.
questions.distractor_summary: Annual or post-deployment scans are too late, and base images can contain vulnerabilities.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: Load tests must run before each production release and fail the release if p99 latency exceeds 300 ms. What is the best approach?
options: Ask users to report slowness after release
Run load tests manually twice a year
Run a load testing stage, for example with Distributed Load Testing on AWS or an open-source tool in CodeBuild, and evaluate results with a gating script
questions.correct_rationale: Automated load tests with a pass or fail gate catch performance regressions before release.
questions.distractor_summary: User reports and manual tests are late, and CPU alarms do not measure latency percentiles.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: What does static application security testing (SAST) do?
options: Tests the running application by sending requests
Analyzes source code for security flaws without running the application
Scans running EC2 instances for open ports
questions.correct_rationale: SAST inspects code during the build to find vulnerabilities early.
questions.distractor_summary: Dynamic testing sends requests to a running app, load testing measures performance, and port scans test infrastructure.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A team wants AI-assisted code review comments on pull requests to catch security and quality issues automatically. Which AWS capability fits best?
options: Amazon Q Developer code reviews integrated with the repository
questions.correct_rationale: Amazon Q Developer can review code and flag security and quality issues.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services provide compliance documents, speech, and data transfer.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Build and manage artifacts
questions.question: A company wants immutable, versioned container images that cannot be overwritten once pushed. What should it configure?
options: Use the latest tag for every build
Enable tag immutability on the Amazon ECR repository
Store images in S3 as tar files with versioning off
questions.correct_rationale: Tag immutability prevents image tags from being overwritten.
questions.distractor_summary: Reusing latest overwrites versions, unversioned S3 copies can be replaced, and deleting images breaks rollbacks.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Build and manage artifacts
questions.question: Which ECR feature removes old or untagged images automatically?
questions.correct_rationale: Lifecycle policies expire images based on age or count.
questions.distractor_summary: Replication copies images, pull-through cache mirrors public images, and repository policies control access.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Build and manage artifacts
questions.question: Deployments in three Regions must pull the same container images with low latency. What should be configured?
options: Pull images from one Region for all deployments
Rebuild images separately in each Region
Store images in an EFS file system
ECR cross-Region replication to repositories in each deployment Region
questions.correct_rationale: Replication keeps identical images close to each Region's deployments.
questions.distractor_summary: Cross-Region pulls add latency and dependency, separate rebuilds can differ, and EFS is not a registry.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Build and manage artifacts
questions.question: A team builds a Java library and wants other teams to consume specific versions through Maven. Where should the artifacts be published?
questions.correct_rationale: CodeArtifact supports Maven, npm, PyPI, NuGet, and other package formats.
questions.distractor_summary: ECR stores container images, Parameter Store holds configuration values, and CloudFront delivers content.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Build and manage artifacts
questions.question: Why should a pipeline build an artifact once and promote the same artifact through environments?
options: It reduces the number of AWS accounts needed
It removes the need for testing
It guarantees that what was tested is exactly what is deployed to production
It makes builds slower on purpose
questions.correct_rationale: Rebuilding per environment can produce different outputs, so promotion of one artifact keeps parity.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not affect account count, testing is still required, and it does not slow builds.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Build and manage artifacts
questions.question: A company uses EC2 Image Builder. What is the main benefit?
options: Manual creation of AMIs from running servers
Automated pipelines that build, test, and distribute hardened AMIs or container images on a schedule
Automatic deletion of all old instances
questions.correct_rationale: Image Builder automates golden image creation and testing.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual AMIs are inconsistent, Marketplace AMIs are separate, and it does not delete instances.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Build and manage artifacts
questions.question: Developers need to use public npm packages, but security requires that only cached, approved versions are used in builds. What fits best?
options: A CodeArtifact repository with an upstream connection to npm, with package origin controls blocking unapproved versions
Let builds download directly from the public registry
Copy node_modules into the repository by hand
Store packages in a public S3 bucket
questions.correct_rationale: CodeArtifact caches public packages and can control which versions are allowed.
questions.distractor_summary: Direct downloads skip controls, manual copies are hard to maintain, and public buckets are unsafe.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Build and manage artifacts
questions.question: What is the purpose of image signing for container images, for example with AWS Signer?
options: Verifying that images come from a trusted publisher and have not been changed
questions.correct_rationale: Signatures let deployment systems verify image integrity and origin.
questions.distractor_summary: Signing does not compress, encrypt, or accelerate images.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Build and manage artifacts
questions.question: Lambda deployments use zip files built in CodeBuild. Where should artifacts be stored for CloudFormation to deploy them?
options: In the CodeBuild container after it stops
In an S3 bucket referenced by the template, for example with sam package or aws cloudformation package
questions.correct_rationale: CloudFormation reads Lambda code from S3 locations produced by the package step.
questions.distractor_summary: Build containers are discarded, environment variables cannot hold code packages, and log groups are not artifact stores.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: An EC2 Auto Scaling group must be updated to a new AMI with no downtime and automatic rollback if instances fail health checks. What fits best?
options: Terminate all instances and let Auto Scaling replace them at once
Update the AMI ID and wait for natural scale-in
An instance refresh with a minimum healthy percentage, checkpoints, and auto rollback, or a CodeDeploy blue/green deployment
Patch instances manually one by one
questions.correct_rationale: Instance refresh replaces instances gradually and can roll back on failure.
questions.distractor_summary: Terminating everything causes downtime, waiting for scale-in is unpredictable, and manual patching is slow.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: In a CodeDeploy EC2 deployment, which file maps lifecycle event hooks to scripts?
questions.correct_rationale: appspec.yml defines files to copy and scripts for hooks such as BeforeInstall and ValidateService.
questions.distractor_summary: buildspec.yml is for CodeBuild, package.json is for Node projects, and Procfile is used by other platforms.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: An ECS service behind an ALB uses rolling updates, and bad releases are discovered only after all tasks are replaced. What is a better strategy?
options: Use ECS blue/green deployments with linear or canary traffic shifting and CloudWatch alarm rollback
Increase the number of tasks updated at once
Deploy only at night without monitoring
questions.correct_rationale: Gradual traffic shifting exposes few users first and rolls back automatically on alarms.
questions.distractor_summary: Larger batches increase impact, disabling circuit breakers removes protection, and unmonitored deploys hide failures.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: What does the ECS deployment circuit breaker do?
options: Stops a rolling deployment that cannot reach a steady state and can roll back to the last working version
questions.correct_rationale: The circuit breaker detects failed deployments and optionally rolls back.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not encrypt, limit CPU, or schedule deployments.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: A Lambda-based API must shift traffic to a new version 10 percent every minute until complete, with automatic rollback on errors. Which configuration fits best?
options: Update the function code in place with no alias
Create a new API Gateway stage for each version
Use reserved concurrency to control traffic
CodeDeploy with the Linear10PercentEvery1Minute deployment configuration and CloudWatch alarms
questions.correct_rationale: Linear deployments shift traffic in fixed steps, and alarms trigger rollback.
questions.distractor_summary: In-place updates switch everyone at once, new stages need clients to change, and concurrency limits do not split traffic.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: A company runs Elastic Beanstalk and needs zero-downtime deployments where a failed deployment never affects the current instances. Which policy fits best?
options: Immutable deployments, or blue/green using a cloned environment and CNAME swap
questions.correct_rationale: Immutable deployments launch new instances in a temporary group, so failures do not touch existing instances.
questions.distractor_summary: All at once and full-batch rolling update every instance, and skipping health checks hides failures.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: What is a canary release?
options: Releasing to all users at once
Releasing a new version to a small portion of users or traffic before a full rollout
Releasing only to the operations team forever
questions.correct_rationale: Canary releases limit risk by testing changes with a small subset first.
questions.distractor_summary: The other options do not describe a progressive release.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: During an EC2 blue/green deployment with CodeDeploy, the team wants old instances kept for one hour in case of rollback. What should be configured?
options: Set the termination wait time for the original instances in the blue/green deployment settings
Keep both fleets serving traffic permanently
questions.correct_rationale: CodeDeploy can wait a set time before terminating the original environment.
questions.distractor_summary: Disabling rollback or terminating early removes the safety net, and running both fleets permanently wastes money.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: Feature flags must allow turning features on for 5 percent of users without redeploying, with safe validation of configuration changes. Which AWS service fits best?
options: AWS AppConfig feature flags with validators and gradual deployment strategies
A text file on each server
An S3 bucket read only at startup
questions.correct_rationale: AppConfig deploys configuration gradually with validation and rollback.
questions.distractor_summary: Redeploying for flags is slow, local files drift, and startup-only reads need restarts.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: A containerized app on EKS needs progressive delivery with automated analysis of metrics. Which approach fits best?
options: Delete and recreate all pods at once
Use kubectl apply manually with no checks
Scale the deployment to zero during releases
Use a progressive delivery controller, such as Argo Rollouts or Flagger, with canary analysis on Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus metrics
questions.correct_rationale: Progressive delivery tools shift traffic gradually and roll back based on metrics.
questions.distractor_summary: Recreating all pods causes outages, manual applies lack checks, and scaling to zero stops service.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: Which CloudFormation feature lets you preview changes to a stack before applying them?
questions.correct_rationale: Change sets show which resources will be added, modified, or replaced.
questions.distractor_summary: Stack policies prevent updates to resources, drift detection compares live state, and termination protection prevents deletion.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: A team deploys a SAM application and wants gradual Lambda deployments defined in the template. What should it add?
options: A separate Lambda function per version with different names
A manual approval inside the function code
An AutoPublishAlias and a DeploymentPreference section with a type such as Canary10Percent5Minutes and alarms
A CloudFront distribution in front of Lambda
questions.correct_rationale: SAM integrates with CodeDeploy for gradual deployments through DeploymentPreference.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate functions break routing, approvals in code are not deployment controls, and CloudFront does not manage function versions.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: A deployment must update a database schema and application together. The team wants rollback to be safe. Which approach fits best?
options: Drop old columns in the same release as the new code
Use backward-compatible schema changes deployed before the application change (expand and contract), so either version works during rollout
questions.correct_rationale: Expand and contract keeps old and new versions compatible, which makes rollback safe.
questions.distractor_summary: Dropping columns breaks rollback, peak-hour renames cause outages, and skipping pipeline changes creates drift.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Implement CI/CD pipelines
questions.question: A pipeline must deploy the same CloudFormation template to five Regions in one stage. Which approach is simplest?
options: Add CloudFormation deploy actions for each Region in the same stage, using cross-Region artifact buckets configured for the pipeline
Create five separate pipelines triggered manually
Deploy to one Region and copy resources with snapshots
Use a single action that deploys to all Regions at once without Regional artifact stores
questions.correct_rationale: CodePipeline supports cross-Region actions when an artifact store exists in each target Region.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate manual pipelines lose consistency, snapshots do not deploy stacks, and cross-Region actions need Regional artifact stores.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Implement deployment strategies for instance, container, and serverless environments
questions.question: A company wants deployments to EC2 instances in an on-premises data center and in AWS using the same tool. Which service fits best?
options: AWS CodeDeploy with on-premises instances registered alongside EC2 instances
questions.correct_rationale: CodeDeploy supports both EC2 and registered on-premises servers.
questions.distractor_summary: Elastic Beanstalk, App Runner, and Fargate run only in AWS.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: Several teams copy the same VPC and logging resources into their templates, and fixes must be repeated everywhere. What should the platform team provide?
options: A wiki page with copy-paste snippets
A single giant template that every team edits
Reusable components, such as AWS CDK constructs or CloudFormation modules, published for teams to import
questions.correct_rationale: Shared constructs or modules let fixes propagate when teams update versions.
questions.distractor_summary: Snippets and console instructions drift, and one shared template creates conflicts.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: Which CloudFormation feature prevents accidental updates to specific critical resources in a stack, such as a production database?
questions.correct_rationale: Stack policies deny update actions on named resources unless explicitly overridden.
questions.distractor_summary: Change sets preview changes, wait conditions pause creation, and drift detection reports differences.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: A stack update replaced an RDS instance and data was lost. How can the team prevent data loss if a future update requires replacement?
options: Set DeletionPolicy and UpdateReplacePolicy to Snapshot or Retain on the database resource and review change sets for replacements
Use only manual console changes for databases
questions.correct_rationale: These policies keep a snapshot or the original resource when CloudFormation would delete or replace it.
questions.distractor_summary: Disabling updates blocks changes, console changes drift, and size has nothing to do with replacement.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: What does CloudFormation drift detection report?
options: Differences between a stack's expected template configuration and the actual resource configuration
questions.correct_rationale: Drift detection identifies resources changed outside CloudFormation.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not report costs, pricing, or IAM credential status.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: A team must pass the VPC ID from a networking stack to many application stacks. What is the standard approach?
options: Export the value as an output from the network stack and import it with Fn::ImportValue, or use SSM parameters
Hard-code the VPC ID in every template
Ask developers to look it up in the console each time
Store it in a Lambda environment variable
questions.correct_rationale: Exports or Parameter Store values share identifiers between stacks reliably.
questions.distractor_summary: Hard-coding and manual lookups break when values change, and a Lambda variable is not a shared reference.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: A CloudFormation template needs a value that is created by a custom process, such as looking up an AMI from an internal service. What should be used?
options: A condition with a fixed string
A custom resource backed by a Lambda function
questions.correct_rationale: Custom resources run code during stack operations and return values to the template.
questions.distractor_summary: Stack policies protect resources, fixed conditions cannot call services, and DeletionPolicy controls deletion.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: Which AWS CDK command shows the CloudFormation changes a deployment would make?
questions.correct_rationale: cdk diff compares the synthesized template with the deployed stack.
questions.distractor_summary: bootstrap prepares an environment, init creates a project, and destroy deletes stacks.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: A company wants approved, versioned infrastructure products that developers can launch with limited permissions. What fits best?
options: Developers with AdministratorAccess using any template
AWS Service Catalog products backed by CloudFormation templates with launch constraints
A shared S3 bucket of unreviewed templates
questions.correct_rationale: Service Catalog offers governed, versioned self-service with launch roles.
questions.distractor_summary: Admin access and unreviewed templates remove governance, and tickets are slow.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: Terraform state for production is stored on a developer laptop, and two engineers corrupted it by running plans at the same time. What should be configured on AWS?
options: Email the state file between engineers
An S3 backend with versioning and state locking (S3 native locking or a DynamoDB lock table)
Store state in a public Git repository
questions.correct_rationale: Remote state with locking prevents concurrent writes and keeps history.
questions.distractor_summary: Emailing and public repositories are unsafe, and Terraform needs state.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: What is a CloudFormation nested stack used for?
options: Reusing common components by referencing one template from another as a resource
Deploying to multiple accounts at once
questions.correct_rationale: Nested stacks let a parent template include child templates for reuse.
questions.distractor_summary: StackSets deploy to many accounts, drift detection is separate, and encryption uses parameters such as dynamic references.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: Templates must never contain database passwords in plain text. How can CloudFormation reference secrets safely?
options: Put the password as a default parameter value
Store the password in the template description
Commit the password to the repository with comments
Use dynamic references to AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store SecureString parameters
questions.correct_rationale: Dynamic references retrieve secrets at deployment time without storing them in templates.
questions.distractor_summary: Defaults, descriptions, and comments expose the secret in plain text.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Deploy automation to create, onboard, and secure AWS accounts in a multi-account or multi-Region environment
questions.question: A company wants new accounts to be created with a baseline of roles, logging, and guardrails automatically when requested. What fits best?
options: A spreadsheet of manual steps per account
Creating accounts with the root user of each new account
AWS Control Tower Account Factory, with Account Factory for Terraform or customizations for baseline resources
Waiting for teams to configure their own accounts
questions.correct_rationale: Account Factory automates provisioning and baselining under governance.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual steps and team self-configuration produce inconsistent accounts, and root use is risky.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Deploy automation to create, onboard, and secure AWS accounts in a multi-account or multi-Region environment
questions.question: A security baseline stack must be deployed to every account in an organization and automatically to accounts added later. Which feature fits best?
options: One stack deployed manually in each account
CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions targeting the organization root or OUs with automatic deployment
questions.correct_rationale: Service-managed StackSets deploy to new accounts as they join target OUs.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual stacks miss new accounts, and aggregators and Access Analyzer do not deploy resources.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Deploy automation to create, onboard, and secure AWS accounts in a multi-account or multi-Region environment
questions.question: What permission model must be set up for self-managed CloudFormation StackSets?
options: Only an IAM user in each target account
An administration role in the administrator account and an execution role in each target account
Service-linked roles created automatically by Organizations
questions.correct_rationale: Self-managed StackSets require the admin and execution roles; service-managed StackSets use Organizations instead.
questions.distractor_summary: IAM users are not the model, roles are required, and automatic service-linked roles apply to service-managed StackSets.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Deploy automation to create, onboard, and secure AWS accounts in a multi-account or multi-Region environment
questions.question: A company needs to enable AWS Config in all accounts and Regions with a standard set of rules. What is the most efficient approach?
options: Deploy conformance packs across the organization from a delegated administrator account
Enable Config manually in each account and Region
Ask teams to create rules on their own
questions.correct_rationale: Organization conformance packs apply standard rules consistently.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual setup is slow and inconsistent, CloudTrail Lake queries activity, and team-created rules vary.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Deploy automation to create, onboard, and secure AWS accounts in a multi-account or multi-Region environment
questions.question: Each new account must have default VPCs deleted in all Regions and a standard VPC created. What is the best automation?
options: Ask account owners to delete default VPCs
Keep default VPCs and ignore them
Run a script once a year
Use Control Tower lifecycle events through EventBridge to trigger a Step Functions or Lambda workflow that removes default VPCs and deploys the baseline
questions.correct_rationale: Event-driven automation reacts to account creation and applies the baseline every time.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual requests and annual scripts are unreliable, and unused default VPCs remain a risk.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Deploy automation to create, onboard, and secure AWS accounts in a multi-account or multi-Region environment
questions.question: Which service lets you run the same Systems Manager Automation runbook across many accounts and Regions?
options: Systems Manager Automation multi-account and multi-Region execution
questions.correct_rationale: Automation can target multiple accounts and Regions with delegated roles.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not run automation.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: A team needs to run a command, such as clearing a cache, on 2,000 instances tagged Environment=Prod, in batches of 10 percent, stopping if errors exceed 2 percent. What fits best?
options: SSH into each instance with a loop script
Systems Manager Run Command targeting by tag with rate control and error thresholds
Use CloudFormation to run the command
questions.correct_rationale: Run Command supports tag targeting with concurrency and error limits.
questions.distractor_summary: SSH loops are slow and need open ports, recreating instances is disruptive, and CloudFormation is not for ad hoc commands.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: Configuration on EC2 instances must be continuously enforced, such as installed agents and file permissions, and automatically corrected. What fits best?
options: Systems Manager State Manager associations applied on a schedule
questions.correct_rationale: State Manager reapplies desired configuration on a schedule to correct drift.
questions.distractor_summary: User data runs once, manual checks miss drift, and Artifact is for compliance documents.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: Which Systems Manager capability stores configuration values and secrets hierarchically, such as /prod/app/db-url?
questions.correct_rationale: Parameter Store keeps configuration and SecureString secrets with hierarchical paths.
questions.distractor_summary: The other capabilities provide access, patching, and fleet management.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: Operations must create golden AMIs monthly with the latest patches and share them with 30 accounts. What fits best?
options: EC2 Image Builder pipelines with distribution settings that share AMIs to target accounts
Manual AMI creation and emailing AMI IDs
Copying EBS volumes to each account by hand
questions.correct_rationale: Image Builder automates builds, tests, and distribution to accounts and Regions.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual steps are error prone, and never updating AMIs leaves vulnerabilities.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: A company wants to orchestrate a multi-step release that includes database migration, cache warming, and traffic shifting, with human approval and error handling. Which service fits best?
options: A single long-running EC2 cron job
An SNS topic with no subscribers
One Lambda function with a 15-minute timeout for everything
AWS Step Functions with task states, callbacks for approval, and catch blocks
questions.correct_rationale: Step Functions coordinates complex workflows with waits, approvals, and error handling.
questions.distractor_summary: Cron jobs and single functions are fragile and limited, and an SNS topic alone does not orchestrate.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: Which tool validates CloudFormation templates against policy-as-code rules, such as "all S3 buckets must be encrypted", before deployment?
questions.correct_rationale: CloudFormation Guard evaluates templates against declarative rules and can run in pipelines.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services provide compliance documents, chatbots, and data transfer.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: A large fleet uses Auto Scaling, and new instances must register with a configuration server before receiving traffic. What fits best?
options: Register instances manually once a day
Use an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook to pause instances in Pending:Wait while a script or Lambda completes registration
Disable health checks for new instances
questions.correct_rationale: Lifecycle hooks let you run custom actions before instances go into service.
questions.distractor_summary: Daily manual registration is too slow, disabling health checks sends traffic to unready instances, and size is irrelevant.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: Teams want to standardize Kubernetes add-ons and configuration across 50 EKS clusters using Git as the source of truth. Which approach fits best?
options: kubectl commands run by hand on each cluster
GitOps with a tool such as Flux or Argo CD, with cluster configuration stored in Git and reconciled automatically
Store manifests in each engineer's home directory
questions.correct_rationale: GitOps continuously reconciles clusters with the declared state in Git.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual commands drift, recreating clusters is disruptive, and local manifests are not a source of truth.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: A CloudFormation stack creation fails halfway, and the team wants to keep the successfully created resources to debug the failure. What should it use?
options: Disable rollback on failure (or use the preserve successfully provisioned resources option) when creating the stack
Delete the stack and recreate it repeatedly
questions.correct_rationale: Disabling rollback keeps created resources in place so the failure can be investigated.
questions.distractor_summary: Recreating hides the cause, and termination protection and stack policies do not stop rollback.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: EC2 instances launched by CloudFormation must finish installing software before the stack reports success. What should be used?
options: A DependsOn on an unrelated resource
A longer stack timeout without signals
A CreationPolicy with cfn-signal sent from the instance after setup completes
questions.correct_rationale: CreationPolicy makes CloudFormation wait for success signals from the instance.
questions.distractor_summary: DependsOn only orders creation, timeouts alone do not confirm success, and DeletionPolicy controls deletion.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: What does the AWS CDK bootstrap process do?
options: Creates resources such as an S3 bucket, ECR repository, and IAM roles that CDK uses to deploy into an account and Region
questions.correct_rationale: Bootstrapping prepares an environment with the assets and roles CDK deployments need.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete stacks, convert to Terraform, or enable Config.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Define cloud infrastructure and reusable components to provision and manage systems throughout their lifecycle
questions.question: An organization must ensure every CloudFormation-created S3 bucket has encryption and versioning, even if a template omits them. Which proactive control fits best?
options: CloudFormation Hooks that check resources before creation and fail non-compliant changes
questions.correct_rationale: Hooks evaluate resource configurations during stack operations and can block them.
questions.distractor_summary: Weekly reports and reminders are after the fact, and Cost Explorer covers spending.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Deploy automation to create, onboard, and secure AWS accounts in a multi-account or multi-Region environment
questions.question: Security wants a read-only audit role in every account that the security account can assume. What is the most scalable way to create it?
options: Create the role manually in each account
Deploy the role with a service-managed CloudFormation StackSet to all OUs
Share the security account's root credentials
Use a single IAM user with access keys in every account
questions.correct_rationale: StackSets deploy the same role to all current and future accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual creation does not scale, and shared root or user credentials are insecure.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Deploy automation to create, onboard, and secure AWS accounts in a multi-account or multi-Region environment
questions.question: A company wants to block member accounts from deleting the baseline CloudFormation stacks that enforce security settings. What should be used?
options: An SCP that denies cloudformation:DeleteStack and UpdateStack on stacks with the baseline prefix for non-administrative roles
Termination protection only, which admins in each account can turn off
A tag on the stack named DoNotDelete
questions.correct_rationale: SCPs enforce the restriction across accounts regardless of local admin permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: Local termination protection can be removed by local admins, tags do not enforce anything, and alarms only notify.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: A team must rotate an API key stored in Parameter Store every 30 days and update dependent services automatically. Which design fits best?
options: Rotate the key manually and send an email
Store the key in code and redeploy monthly
An EventBridge Scheduler rule that runs a Step Functions workflow or Lambda function to rotate the value and notify consumers
questions.correct_rationale: Scheduled automation rotates and propagates the value consistently.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual or no rotation is risky, and keys in code are exposed.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: Which Systems Manager feature provides an inventory of installed software and configuration across instances?
questions.correct_rationale: Inventory collects metadata about applications, files, and configuration from managed nodes.
questions.distractor_summary: OpsCenter manages operational issues, Artifact holds reports, and Budgets tracks cost.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Design and build automated solutions for complex tasks and large-scale environments
questions.question: Auto Scaling groups across 20 accounts must use the latest approved AMI without editing each launch template. What fits best?
options: Hard-code AMI IDs in every template and update them by hand
Use the oldest AMI to avoid change
Store the approved AMI ID in a Parameter Store parameter shared across accounts and reference it in launch templates with resolve:ssm
Create a new Auto Scaling group for each AMI
questions.correct_rationale: Launch templates can resolve AMI IDs from Parameter Store, so one update reaches all groups.
questions.distractor_summary: Hard-coded IDs require many edits, old AMIs miss patches, and new groups per AMI add churn.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: A web application runs on EC2 in one Availability Zone. Which change gives the biggest availability improvement?
options: Use a larger instance in the same AZ
Run the Auto Scaling group across at least two AZs behind an Application Load Balancer
questions.correct_rationale: Spreading instances across AZs survives the loss of one AZ.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigger instances and extra volumes share the same AZ, and monitoring does not add redundancy.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: An ECS service on Fargate must keep running if an AZ fails, with enough capacity left to serve full load. How should tasks be configured?
options: Spread tasks across three AZs and set the desired count so the remaining two AZs can carry full load
Run all tasks in one AZ for lower latency
Use one task with maximum CPU
Spread tasks across two AZs with capacity for only half the load
questions.correct_rationale: Over-provisioning across AZs keeps full capacity after losing one AZ.
questions.distractor_summary: Single-AZ or single-task designs fail with the AZ, and half capacity overloads the survivors.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: What does Amazon RDS Multi-AZ (one standby) provide?
options: A synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover
questions.correct_rationale: The standby receives synchronous replication and takes over during failures.
questions.distractor_summary: The single standby does not serve reads, it is in the same Region, and it does not shard.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: A DynamoDB-based application needs to survive a Regional outage with writes possible in either Region. What fits best?
options: A larger provisioned capacity in one Region
DynamoDB global tables in two Regions with Route 53 or application-level failover
questions.correct_rationale: Global tables provide multi-Region, multi-active replication.
questions.distractor_summary: PITR restores in Region, capacity does not cover a Region outage, and DAX is a cache.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: A stateful legacy application can run on only one instance at a time but must recover quickly if that instance fails. What is a simple resilient design?
options: A single instance with no Auto Scaling
Two instances running at the same time writing to local disks
An Auto Scaling group with min and max of 1 across multiple AZs, with data on Amazon EFS or a database rather than local disk
An instance store-backed instance with daily manual copies
questions.correct_rationale: A self-healing group of one replaces the instance in another AZ, and shared storage keeps data.
questions.distractor_summary: A lone instance does not recover, two writers conflict, and instance store loses data.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: Which load balancer type is best for extreme TCP performance with static IP addresses per AZ?
questions.correct_rationale: NLBs work at layer 4 with very high throughput and support static or Elastic IPs.
questions.distractor_summary: ALBs work at layer 7, Classic is legacy, and Gateway Load Balancer is for appliances.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: A team wants Route 53 to stop sending traffic to an endpoint that returns HTTP 500 errors. What should be configured?
options: Route 53 health checks on the endpoint's health URL associated with the records
A simple routing policy without health checks
A CNAME at the zone apex
questions.correct_rationale: Health checks remove unhealthy endpoints from DNS answers for supported routing policies.
questions.distractor_summary: Longer TTLs slow changes, simple routing ignores health, and CNAMEs are not allowed at the apex.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: A Lambda function processing SQS messages fails on certain malformed messages, which block the queue processing for that batch repeatedly. What improves resilience?
options: Configure a dead-letter queue (redrive policy) and enable partial batch responses (ReportBatchItemFailures)
Increase the function timeout to 15 minutes
Delete the queue and recreate it daily
Remove error handling from the function
questions.correct_rationale: Partial batch responses retry only failed messages, and the DLQ isolates repeated failures.
questions.distractor_summary: Longer timeouts do not fix bad data, recreating queues loses messages, and less error handling makes it worse.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement solutions that are scalable to meet business requirements
questions.question: Traffic to an application increases every weekday at 9 AM. Instances take 5 minutes to warm up, causing slow responses. What fits best?
options: Disable scaling and run at peak all day
Use step scaling with a 30-minute cooldown
Wait for users to complain, then scale manually
Add scheduled scaling before 9 AM or predictive scaling, and use a warm pool for faster launches
questions.correct_rationale: Scaling ahead of known peaks and warm pools avoid slow starts.
questions.distractor_summary: Running at peak all day wastes money, long cooldowns react slowly, and manual scaling is late.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement solutions that are scalable to meet business requirements
questions.question: Which Auto Scaling policy keeps a metric, such as average CPU, near a target value?
questions.correct_rationale: Target tracking adjusts capacity to hold a metric at the target.
questions.distractor_summary: Simple scaling uses one adjustment per alarm, scheduled scaling uses times, and manual scaling needs a person.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement solutions that are scalable to meet business requirements
questions.question: A worker fleet consumes jobs from SQS. Scaling on CPU lags behind queue growth. What metric should drive scaling?
options: Disk space used on each instance
Backlog per instance, calculated from ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible divided by running instances, with target tracking
questions.correct_rationale: Backlog per instance relates queue depth to capacity, so the fleet scales with the work waiting.
questions.distractor_summary: Network, disk, and IAM counts do not reflect queued work.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement solutions that are scalable to meet business requirements
questions.question: A read-heavy Aurora cluster sees spikes in read traffic. How can read capacity scale automatically?
options: Enable Aurora Auto Scaling for replicas based on CPU or connections
questions.correct_rationale: Aurora Auto Scaling adds and removes replicas as load changes.
questions.distractor_summary: Aurora clusters have one writer in standard configurations, backups do not add read capacity, and magnetic storage is slower.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement solutions that are scalable to meet business requirements
questions.question: Which DynamoDB capacity mode scales instantly to accommodate traffic without capacity planning?
questions.correct_rationale: On-demand mode handles changing traffic without setting capacity.
questions.distractor_summary: Fixed provisioned capacity does not scale, reserved capacity is a pricing option, and table class affects storage cost.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement solutions that are scalable to meet business requirements
questions.question: A Lambda function behind API Gateway is throttled during spikes, and other functions in the account are starved of concurrency. What should be done?
options: Set reserved concurrency to zero on all functions
Set reserved concurrency for critical functions and request an account concurrency quota increase if needed
questions.correct_rationale: Reserved concurrency protects critical functions, and quotas can be raised for overall demand.
questions.distractor_summary: Zero reserved concurrency stops functions, memory does not change concurrency limits, and removing throttling can overload backends.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement solutions that are scalable to meet business requirements
questions.question: A containerized service on EKS must scale nodes automatically to fit pending pods. What fits best?
options: Fixed node groups sized for average load
Karpenter or the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler, or EKS Auto Mode
questions.correct_rationale: Node autoscalers add capacity when pods cannot be scheduled.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual and fixed sizing do not react to demand, and restarting the control plane does not add nodes.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: The business requires an RPO of 5 minutes for an RDS for PostgreSQL database within the same Region. What feature meets this?
options: Automated backups with point-in-time recovery, which can restore to within about five minutes of the latest restorable time
Read replicas in the same AZ
questions.correct_rationale: PITR uses transaction logs uploaded frequently, enabling recovery close to the failure time.
questions.distractor_summary: Weekly snapshots miss the RPO, Multi-AZ does not protect against logical errors, and same-AZ replicas share failures.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: A company must recover from accidental deletion of DynamoDB items within the last 35 days. What should be enabled?
questions.correct_rationale: PITR allows restores to any second in the retention window.
questions.distractor_summary: Streams keep 24 hours of changes, global tables replicate deletions, and DAX is a cache.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: What is the purpose of regularly testing disaster recovery runbooks?
options: To prove that RTO and RPO targets can actually be met and to find gaps before a real disaster
To increase AWS costs on purpose
questions.correct_rationale: Testing validates recovery procedures and timing.
questions.distractor_summary: Testing does not replace backups and is not a pricing activity.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: An Auto Scaling group should replace instances that fail a custom application health check script. How can this be done?
options: Have the script call SetInstanceHealth to mark the instance Unhealthy so Auto Scaling replaces it
Increase the health check grace period to one day
questions.correct_rationale: Custom health status lets Auto Scaling replace instances based on application logic.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual stops are slow, deleting the group causes outages, and long grace periods delay replacement.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: A company uses AWS Backup and must prove that restores work each month without manual effort. What fits best?
options: Assume backups work because jobs succeed
Copy backups to a second vault only
AWS Backup restore testing plans that restore recovery points on a schedule and validate them
questions.correct_rationale: Restore testing automates periodic restores to verify recoverability.
questions.distractor_summary: Successful backup jobs do not prove restores, annual tests are infrequent, and copying does not test restores.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: Which EC2 feature automatically recovers an instance onto new hardware if the underlying host fails, keeping the instance ID and IP?
options: EC2 instance auto recovery (simplified automatic recovery or a CloudWatch recover action)
questions.correct_rationale: Automatic recovery migrates the instance to healthy hardware while keeping its identity.
questions.distractor_summary: Hibernation saves memory state, Spot notices warn of interruptions, and Instance Connect is for SSH.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Configure the collection, aggregation, and storage of logs and metrics
questions.question: A team needs memory and disk usage metrics from EC2 instances, which are not collected by default. What should it install?
options: The CloudWatch agent with a configuration that collects memory and disk metrics
questions.correct_rationale: The CloudWatch agent collects OS-level metrics and logs not available from the hypervisor.
questions.distractor_summary: X-Ray traces requests, Inspector scans vulnerabilities, and Config tracks configuration.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Configure the collection, aggregation, and storage of logs and metrics
questions.question: Application logs from 30 accounts must be streamed to a central account for analysis in near real time. What fits best?
options: Daily exports to S3 in each account
CloudWatch Logs subscription filters to a destination in the central account backed by Kinesis Data Streams or Amazon Data Firehose
Increase log retention in each account
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-account subscriptions stream log events continuously to a central pipeline.
questions.distractor_summary: Daily exports are not near real time, manual downloads do not scale, and retention does not centralize logs.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Configure the collection, aggregation, and storage of logs and metrics
questions.question: What does a CloudWatch Logs metric filter do?
options: Turns matching log patterns into CloudWatch metrics that can drive alarms
Deletes logs that match a pattern
questions.correct_rationale: Metric filters count or extract values from logs to create metrics.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not delete, encrypt, or export logs.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Configure the collection, aggregation, and storage of logs and metrics
questions.question: Logs must be retained for 7 years cheaply, but are rarely read after 30 days. What fits best?
options: Keep all logs in CloudWatch Logs forever
Set CloudWatch Logs retention to 30 days and archive logs to S3 with lifecycle transitions to Glacier classes
questions.correct_rationale: Short CloudWatch retention plus S3 archiving keeps long-term storage cheap.
questions.distractor_summary: Keeping everything in CloudWatch is costly, EBS snapshots are unsuitable, and deletion breaks retention.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Configure the collection, aggregation, and storage of logs and metrics
questions.question: A microservices platform needs distributed traces and metrics using open standards so it can switch vendors later. Which approach fits best?
options: Write custom logging in each service with different formats
Instrument with OpenTelemetry using the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry and send data to X-Ray and CloudWatch
questions.correct_rationale: OpenTelemetry gives vendor-neutral instrumentation, and ADOT exports to AWS backends.
questions.distractor_summary: Custom formats are inconsistent, flow logs show network metadata, and CloudTrail records API calls.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Configure the collection, aggregation, and storage of logs and metrics
questions.question: Which log type records IP traffic metadata for network interfaces in a VPC?
questions.correct_rationale: Flow Logs capture accepted and rejected traffic metadata.
questions.distractor_summary: CloudTrail records API calls, S3 access logs record bucket requests, and Config records configuration.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Configure the collection, aggregation, and storage of logs and metrics
questions.question: A team wants high-resolution metrics at 1-second granularity for a latency-sensitive service. What should it publish?
options: High-resolution custom metrics with a storage resolution of 1 second
questions.correct_rationale: High-resolution metrics support 1-second data points.
questions.distractor_summary: Basic metrics are coarser, billing metrics track cost, and CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API activity.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 Configure the collection, aggregation, and storage of logs and metrics
questions.question: Container logs from ECS on Fargate must go to both CloudWatch Logs and a third-party system with routing rules. What fits best?
options: Use the FireLens log router (Fluent Bit) as a sidecar with outputs to both destinations
SSH into each task to copy logs
Write logs to the container file system
questions.correct_rationale: FireLens routes container logs to multiple destinations with filters.
questions.distractor_summary: awslogs sends only to CloudWatch, Fargate tasks have no SSH, and local files are lost.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Audit, monitor, and analyze logs and metrics to detect issues
questions.question: Engineers need to query recent application logs to find the top error messages during an incident. Which tool fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: Logs Insights runs interactive queries over log groups.
questions.distractor_summary: The others do not query logs.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: An application caches session data in a single ElastiCache node. When the node fails, all users are logged out. What should be configured?
options: A second cluster in the same AZ with no replication
A replication group with replicas in other AZs and Multi-AZ automatic failover
questions.correct_rationale: Replicas with automatic failover keep the cache available during node or AZ failures.
questions.distractor_summary: A larger node still fails as one, snapshots do not give live failover, and unreplicated clusters lose data.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: What is the purpose of cross-zone load balancing?
options: Distributing traffic evenly across registered targets in all enabled Availability Zones
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-zone load balancing spreads requests across targets in every AZ, not just the AZ that received them.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not route between Regions, encrypt traffic, or block AZs.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Implement highly available solutions to meet resilience and business requirements
questions.question: An application uses an Amazon EFS file system and must recover from a Regional failure with an RPO of minutes. What should be configured?
options: EFS replication to a file system in another Region
Daily rsync to an EC2 instance in the same Region
questions.correct_rationale: EFS replication keeps a read-only copy in another Region with a low RPO and allows failover.
questions.distractor_summary: One Zone reduces resilience, same-Region copies do not cover Regional failure, and lifecycle only changes storage class.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement solutions that are scalable to meet business requirements
questions.question: A Kinesis Data Streams consumer falls behind during peak hours. The stream uses provisioned mode. What can increase throughput?
options: Increase the shard count or switch to on-demand capacity mode, and use enhanced fan-out for multiple consumers
Use a smaller record size only
Add more partitions in the producer without changing shards
questions.correct_rationale: More shards or on-demand mode raise capacity, and enhanced fan-out gives each consumer dedicated throughput.
questions.distractor_summary: Retention does not affect throughput, record size alone is not enough, and producer partitions do not create shards.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Implement solutions that are scalable to meet business requirements
questions.question: Which feature of Application Load Balancer allows routing requests to different target groups based on URL path?
questions.correct_rationale: Listener rules can forward /api to one target group and /images to another.
questions.distractor_summary: The other features control distribution, deregistration, and session affinity.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: A company's pilot light DR environment requires 2 hours of manual steps to scale up. The RTO is 30 minutes. What should be done?
options: Document the manual steps more clearly
Extend the RTO without telling the business
Automate the failover with infrastructure as code and a runbook, for example Systems Manager Automation or Step Functions, and test it regularly
questions.correct_rationale: Automated, tested failover reduces recovery time to meet the RTO.
questions.distractor_summary: Better documentation still leaves manual delays, and the other options abandon the requirement.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: Which AWS service orchestrates cross-Region application recovery with readiness checks and routing controls?
questions.correct_rationale: ARC provides readiness checks and highly available routing controls for failover.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not orchestrate recovery.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: What is the main difference between RTO and RPO?
options: RTO measures data loss and RPO measures downtime
RTO is how long recovery may take, while RPO is how much data loss, in time, is acceptable
Both measure the cost of recovery
questions.correct_rationale: RTO and RPO define recovery time and data loss tolerance.
questions.distractor_summary: The terms are not about cost or latency, and they are not reversed.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Implement automated recovery processes to meet RTO and RPO requirements
questions.question: Backups are taken, but nobody knows how long a full restore takes. What should be done first to validate the RTO?
options: Perform and time a full restore test in a non-production environment
questions.correct_rationale: Only a real restore test shows the actual recovery time.
questions.distractor_summary: More frequent backups affect RPO, storage and names do not measure RTO.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Audit, monitor, and analyze logs and metrics to detect issues
questions.question: A team wants alarms that do not fire on a single brief spike but alert when errors stay high. How should the alarm be configured?
options: Set evaluation periods and datapoints to alarm, for example 3 out of 5 periods
Use a 1-out-of-1 rule with a 10-second period
Disable the alarm during business hours
questions.correct_rationale: M out of N evaluation filters out short spikes while catching sustained problems.
questions.distractor_summary: Single-datapoint alarms are noisy, disabling alarms hides issues, and statistics alone do not handle duration.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Audit, monitor, and analyze logs and metrics to detect issues
questions.question: A service's normal traffic varies by hour and day, making static thresholds noisy. What should be used?
options: A fixed threshold set to the highest value ever seen
CloudWatch anomaly detection alarms based on a learned baseline
questions.correct_rationale: Anomaly detection models expected values and alerts on deviations.
questions.distractor_summary: Fixed high thresholds miss problems, no alarms hides failures, and billing alarms track cost.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Audit, monitor, and analyze logs and metrics to detect issues
questions.question: Which CloudWatch feature combines several alarms into one alarm using AND and OR logic to reduce alert noise?
questions.correct_rationale: Composite alarms trigger based on the state of other alarms.
questions.distractor_summary: Metric math computes values, Contributor Insights finds top contributors, and dashboards display data.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Audit, monitor, and analyze logs and metrics to detect issues
questions.question: An operations team wants to identify which client IPs generate the most 5xx errors from application logs. Which feature fits best?
options: CloudWatch Contributor Insights rules on the log group
questions.correct_rationale: Contributor Insights shows top contributors to a metric pattern in logs.
questions.distractor_summary: The other tools do not analyze log contributors.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Audit, monitor, and analyze logs and metrics to detect issues
questions.question: A company must detect unusual API activity, such as a sudden spike in TerminateInstances calls, across its accounts. What fits best?
options: CloudTrail Insights on the organization trail, with EventBridge notifications
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail Insights detects unusual write API call volumes and error rates.
questions.distractor_summary: Flow Logs, S3 access logs, and memory metrics do not analyze API call patterns.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Audit, monitor, and analyze logs and metrics to detect issues
questions.question: What does AWS X-Ray's service map show?
options: The services in a request path and their latency, errors, and faults
questions.correct_rationale: The service map visualizes how components connect and where errors occur.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not show billing, IAM, or ACLs.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Audit, monitor, and analyze logs and metrics to detect issues
questions.question: A team wants to monitor a checkout page from outside AWS every minute and alert on failures. What fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: Canaries run scripts on a schedule to check endpoints and user flows.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services do not run synthetic checks.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 Audit, monitor, and analyze logs and metrics to detect issues
questions.question: A company needs to query CloudTrail events across accounts with SQL for audits, with long retention, without managing a data pipeline. What fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail Lake stores events and supports SQL queries without building pipelines.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual downloads do not scale, dashboards do not run SQL on events, and Trusted Advisor gives checks.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Automate monitoring and event management of complex environments
questions.question: When a CloudWatch alarm fires for high error rates, the team wants an automated runbook to collect diagnostics and post to chat. What fits best?
options: Wait for someone to notice the dashboard
Email the alarm to a shared mailbox nobody reads
Route the alarm through EventBridge or SNS to a Systems Manager Automation runbook and Amazon Q Developer in chat applications
questions.correct_rationale: Event-driven automation gathers data immediately and notifies the team in chat.
questions.distractor_summary: Waiting, unread mailboxes, and disabling alarms delay response.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Automate monitoring and event management of complex environments
questions.question: Which service enables CloudWatch alarms to show up in Slack or Microsoft Teams channels?
options: Amazon Q Developer in chat applications (formerly AWS Chatbot)
questions.correct_rationale: This integration delivers notifications to chat channels and allows some commands.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact provides reports, SES sends email, and Budgets tracks spending.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Automate monitoring and event management of complex environments
questions.question: Dashboards and alarms must be created automatically whenever a new microservice is deployed. What is the best approach?
options: Define dashboards and alarms in the service's infrastructure as code template so they deploy with the service
Ask the operations team to build them by hand later
Create one dashboard for all services manually each quarter
questions.correct_rationale: Monitoring as code ensures every service ships with consistent observability.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual or delayed creation leaves gaps, and skipping monitoring hides failures.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Automate monitoring and event management of complex environments
questions.question: A team wants an automatic response when EC2 instances show high CPU credit exhaustion on burstable types. What fits best?
options: An alarm on CPUCreditBalance that triggers an EventBridge rule or automation to switch to unlimited mode or a larger type
A manual weekly review of instance types
Moving instances to a different Region
questions.correct_rationale: Alarms plus automation respond to credit exhaustion quickly.
questions.distractor_summary: Weekly reviews are slow, removing metrics hides the problem, and changing Regions does not fix it.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Automate monitoring and event management of complex environments
questions.question: Which AWS service gives a consolidated view of resource health and events affecting your account, and can send events to EventBridge?
questions.correct_rationale: AWS Health provides account-specific events that can trigger EventBridge rules.
questions.distractor_summary: The other services address compliance documents, licenses, and sensitive data.

questions.subdomain: 4.3 Automate monitoring and event management of complex environments
questions.question: A team uses Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus for EKS metrics. Which service should it use to build dashboards on those metrics?
questions.correct_rationale: Managed Grafana connects to Prometheus and other sources for operational dashboards.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact, QuickSight, and Budgets are not suited for Prometheus operational dashboards.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 Manage event sources to process, notify, and take action in response to events
questions.question: When an EC2 instance changes to the stopped state unexpectedly in production, a Lambda function must record the event and notify the on-call team. What fits best?
options: A cron job that lists instances every hour
An EventBridge rule matching EC2 state-change events targeting Lambda and SNS
